audits.title: An audit to assess whether patients under the care of a community mental health team who are taking clozapine are having their lipid profile checked annually and are given lifestyle advice and have had a QRISK3 assessment
audits.standard: NICE: lipids at baseline, 3 months after starting a new antipsychotic, then annually; lifestyle advice and QRISK3 assessment
audits.setting: Community mental health team, Cardiff and Vale University Health Board

cycle1.result: 36/39 (92%) had lipids checked in 12 months; 21/39 (54%) cholesterol over 5.0; 9/39 (23%) documented lifestyle discussion; 0/39 (0%) QRISK3 assessment.

audits.other_findings: 17 of 56 patients excluded as on cholesterol-lowering medication. Teaching on lifestyle advice and QRISK3 planned.
audits.citation: Linley-Adams E, Harris B. An audit to assess whether patients under the care of a community mental health team who are taking clozapine are having their lipid profile checked annually and are given lifestyle advice and have had a QRISK3 assessment. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S89-S89.

audits.title: Clinical Audit of Clozapine Prescribing Practice and Monitoring Process in an Australian Community Mental Health Service
audits.standard: Monash Health clozapine patient management guidelines and RANZCP clinical practice guidelines
audits.setting: Community mental health service, Monash Health

cycle1.result: Monthly weight, physical examination, medical review and full blood examination 97% compliant; BMI monitoring 66.7%; six-monthly consultant review 42.4%.

audits.other_findings: Clozapine level subtherapeutic in 54.5% and 54.5% on an adjunct psychotropic; hypersalivation was the commonest side effect (57.6%).
audits.citation: Fernando T, Bhandarkar R, Meadows G. Clinical Audit of Clozapine Prescribing Practice and Monitoring Process in an Australian Community Mental Health Service. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S4-S5.

audits.title: Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Long-Stay Psychiatric Inpatients on Clozapine in NHS Ayrshire & Arran
audits.standard: Scottish Government 2017 National Standard for Monitoring the Physical Health of People Being Treated with Clozapine
audits.setting: Long-stay inpatient forensic and rehabilitation psychiatry services, NHS Ayrshire & Arran

cycle1.result: Fasting glucose in preceding 6 months 10/18; lipid profile 12/18; LFTs within a year 18/18; BMI, heart rate and BP within a year 18/18; ECG within a year 12/18

audits.other_findings: Rehabilitation ward with an existing checklist achieved 100% adherence; a checklist is planned for forensic wards with re-audit in 6 months.
audits.citation: Carson C. Audit of Physical Health Monitoring in Long-Stay Psychiatric Inpatients on Clozapine in NHS Ayrshire & Arran. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S152-S152.

audits.title: Lipid Profile and Cardiovascular Risk Monitoring in Patients on Clozapine – an Audit at a Community Mental Health Resource Centre in Scotland
audits.standard: NICE guidance: lipid profile at baseline, 3 months and annually, and cardiovascular risk assessment with a validated tool (QRISK3 or ASSIGN score)
audits.setting: Community mental health resource centre (local CMHT)

cycle1.result: Lipid profile done in the past 12 months in 22/27 (81.1%); cardiovascular risk assessed in 1/27 (3.70%); lipid results communicated to GP in 4/22 (18.18%).

audits.intervention: Proposed structured process: clozapine clinic nurse creates an electronic task for the medic to review results, calculate cardiovascular risk and communicate lipids and risk to the GP in the annual review letter. Re-audit planned after 12 months.
audits.other_findings: Of 40 patients on clozapine, 13 were excluded (on statins, recently started, or outside age 30–74). Of those tested, 13/22 (59.9%) had total cholesterol above 5 mmol/L.
audits.citation: Shahzad A. Lipid Profile and Cardiovascular Risk Monitoring in Patients on Clozapine – an Audit at a Community Mental Health Resource Centre in Scotland. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S260-S261. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.628.

audits.title: Clozapine Monitoring in Older Adults: An Audit Evaluating Compliance With Clozapine Guidelines in Community Settings
audits.standard: Trust guideline: FBC, glucose, prolactin, U&E, lipids and LFTs every 6 months; HbA1c and clozapine plasma assay annually
audits.setting: Four Older Adult Community Mental Health Teams, Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Full compliance: FBC 100%; HbA1c 100%; LFTs 71%; U&E 57%; clozapine level 43%; glucose 0%; prolactin 0%; lipids 0% (43% had at least one test).

audits.other_findings: Many tests were done by GPs or hospitals for other reasons (e.g. 50% of U&Es, 71% of LFTs); authors suggest considering dedicated clozapine clinics.
audits.citation: Tong G, McCarthy M. Clozapine Monitoring in Older Adults: An Audit Evaluating Compliance With Clozapine Guidelines in Community Settings. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S266-S267. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.640.

audits.title: Improving Clozapine Blood Monitoring in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Targeted Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.standard: Trust guidelines: routine FBCs for all patients on clozapine and clozapine levels only on consultant guidance; target inappropriate tests reduced from 53% to zero by April 2024

cycle1.result: 53% of clozapine-related tests inappropriate, with missed FBCs.

audits.intervention: 20-minute training sessions for nurses on clozapine blood monitoring on three days, plus an aide-memoire at key ward locations.

cycle2.result: FBCs sent routinely for all patients on clozapine; no inappropriate clozapine level requests.

audits.other_findings: Staff confidence in clozapine monitoring increased on pre- and post-training questionnaires. Periodic refresher training was recommended.
audits.citation: Raja S, Lakda A. Improving Clozapine Blood Monitoring in Inpatient Psychiatry: A Targeted Quality Improvement Initiative. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S161-S161. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10429.

audits.title: Myocarditis monitoring during clozapine initiation: audit of practice in an NHS trust.
audits.standard: No standardised framework; evidence-based cardiac monitoring (baseline ECG, weekly troponin and CRP in first 4 weeks, vital signs)
audits.setting: Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust (mental health trust), patients registered to start clozapine

cycle1.result: Of 219 patients, 180 had complete data. Baseline ECG completed in 80%; no routine troponin monitoring identified; CRP testing infrequent.

audits.other_findings: Tachycardia occurred in more than 40%; 15 referred to cardiology before initiation, 6 in first 4 weeks and 5 thereafter; 12 (7%) discontinued clozapine early, mainly owing to tachycardia. Authors propose adding weekly troponin and CRP to mandatory blood tests.
audits.citation: Bridges M, Secchi A, Kumar Y, Nettey VV, Bahia J, Whiskey E, et al.. Myocarditis monitoring during clozapine initiation: audit of practice in an NHS trust. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(5):e216. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.12079. PMID: 42639724.

audits.title: The physical health and side-effect monitoring of patients prescribed clozapine: data from a clinical audit conducted in UK mental health services.
audits.standard: Treatment guideline recommendations for physical health and side-effect monitoring with clozapine
audits.setting: 63 NHS trusts/healthcare organisations, UK mental health services (POMH-UK programme)

cycle1.result: In 481 patients on clozapine up to 18 weeks, pretreatment BP, heart rate and ECG documented in at least 90%; weight, lipids, glucose/HbA1c and examination about 80%; daily heart rate and BP in first 2 weeks 82%, temperature 77%; CRP or CK 42%, troponin or BNP 29%. In 5908 patients on clozapine at least 1 year, BP and weight/BMI at least 80%, lipids 78%, glucose 73%, ECG 55%.

audits.other_findings: Structured side-effect assessment tool used in only 29% of those with weekly assessments; one third with schizophrenia were co-prescribed a second antipsychotic.
audits.citation: Barnes TRE, MacCabe JH, Kane JM, Delgado O, Paton C. The physical health and side-effect monitoring of patients prescribed clozapine: data from a clinical audit conducted in UK mental health services. Ther Adv Psychopharmacol. 2020;10:2045125320937908. doi:10.1177/2045125320937908. PMID: 32821377.

audits.title: Prescribing clozapine in the UK: Quality improvement issues identified by clinical audit.
audits.standard: POMH clozapine practice standards (smoking status in care plan, clozapine in Summary Care Record)
audits.setting: UK NHS mental health trusts, Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health QI programme

cycle1.result: Smoking status change considered in care plans of just under one-third of relevant patients; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 58% of community patients.

audits.intervention: POMH quality improvement programme between audits.

cycle2.result: Smoking status change considered in just over a half; clozapine in Summary Care Record in 72%.

audits.other_findings: In both audits over a quarter of patients had high-dose and/or combined antipsychotics before clozapine was started.
audits.citation: Barnes TR, MacCabe JH, Kane JM, Delgado O, Khan M, Paton C. Prescribing clozapine in the UK: Quality improvement issues identified by clinical audit. J Psychopharmacol. 2022;36(9):1036-1040. doi:10.1177/02698811221104060. PMID: 35695172.

audits.title: Monitoring Troponin I and CRP During Clozapine Titration: Assessing Adherence to Myocarditis Protocols
audits.standard: Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines and Ronaldson algorithm: baseline and weekly troponin and CRP during the first four weeks of clozapine titration
audits.setting: Swallownest Court general adult psychiatry inpatient wards, Rotherham Doncaster and South Humber NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Baseline troponin and CRP documented in 80%, baseline ECG in 90%; 5 (50%) had mildly raised troponin (>3 but <13 ng/L), 80% of these had repeat troponin testing; no suspected myocarditis

audits.intervention: Recommendations to align local practice with Ronaldson and Maudsley protocols using locally agreed reference ranges, to be added to local policy; re-audit planned
audits.other_findings: Repeat troponin tests were often triggered by acute coronary syndrome reference ranges rather than myocarditis thresholds. CRP rose in four patients, two from non-cardiac causes.
audits.citation: Chowdhury T, Martin A. Monitoring Troponin I and CRP During Clozapine Titration: Assessing Adherence to Myocarditis Protocols. BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S175-S175.
